sections.html:
In the Pee Dee corner of northeastern South Carolina, Florence County is anchored by the city of Florence, which is the seat and the biggest community. Johnsonville and Lake City are its other municipalities. Total area is 804.28 square miles, with 800.51 of land, and the 2020 count found 137,059 residents in 54,627 households. Health care leads employment at 22.9 percent, followed by retail at 13.3 percent.

Location inside the county changes what you owe. Houses within the city of Florence also pay city tax, whose rate City Council sets by June 30 each year, so look at each millage line on the bill instead of the county total alone.

Real estate and most personal property taxes come due January 15. If that lands on a weekend or holiday, expect the next business day instead. Notices normally go out around October.

DatePenalty addedTotal
January 163%3%
February 27%10%
March 175%15%, plus collection costs

Calculating the tax and adding penalties is the Auditor's work. The Treasurer collects the entire amount shown on the notice, so a partial payment will be turned away. Postmarks count, and an online outage will not excuse a penalty. A receipt shows the day the payment was processed.

One relief exists in state law. When the house changed hands during the tax year and only the former owner received the notice, the treasurer waives penalties for the new owner. It is a narrow rule, so after any sale confirm the bill's mailing address with the Assessor.

sections.h2: How to pay and who to call
sections.html:
Payments can be made at the counter, by mail or online. Mailed payments go to Florence County Treasurer, P.O. Box 100501, Florence, SC 29502-0501, while the county complex sits at 180 N Irby Street, Florence, SC 29501. Offices there keep weekday hours, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

  • Treasurer: 843-665-3041. Collects the bill and also serves as tax collector.
  • Tax Assessor: 843-665-3056. Legal residence, address changes, mobile home registrations, deeds and plats.
  • Auditor: 843-665-3088. Homestead exemption, bill calculation and penalties.
  • Delinquent Tax Collection: 843-665-3095. Payoff amounts and tax sale redemption.

In person, a card needs ID and a signature and carries a processor fee of 1.7 percent plus $1. PayStar handles online payments for an added fee of its own, and the official receipt comes by mail within 5 to 10 business days. Overdue taxes cannot be paid online; use cash, a cashier's check, a money order or a card at the counter. The county's Treasurer page has the current details.

Each county in South Carolina must reappraise all real property every five years at market value. Within a cycle, taxable value is held to a 15 percent rise over five years unless an assessable transfer of interest occurs, and a sale usually counts as one.

When values rise overall, millage must drop to a rollback rate, although a single bill can still move either way. Any change of $1,000 or more comes with a notice to the owner.

Put an appeal in writing and send it to the Tax Assessor; a PDF form can be downloaded from the county site. Before planning around a deadline, ask which reassessment cycle applies to your parcel. For a dispute outside a notice window, you can object in writing within 90 days after the assessor mails a notice. The county also runs qPublic for parcel records and a tax estimator, so a buyer or seller can get a feel for what a new owner might owe.

For a legal residence application, the Assessor's Office wants to see a South Carolina driver's license or state ID, the vehicle registration, a voter registration card where one applies, and a Social Security card, for both applicant and spouse. The list took effect June 20, 2016.

The Auditor's Office separately runs the Homestead Exemption Program and has an application form. After a sale, a new owner should ask the Assessor how to apply and what date the paperwork must reach the office for the next bill.

The Delinquent Tax Office runs a public auction of unpaid real property. The latest sale started Monday, October 5, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Bidders paid a $10 fee and pre-registered by October 2.

An owner or mortgage holder may redeem for a year and a day, and for parcels in that auction the last day is October 6, 2027. Interest builds by quarter at 3, 6, 9 and 12 percent of the bid. A tax deed goes out if no one redeems, and the county cautions that it is not a warranty deed and liens can survive.

Fees grow as the year goes on. Recent charges include $20 for delinquent notices in March, $30 for certified mail of a levy in April, $25 for advertising in August and $60 for a land mortgage search in October. Call 843-665-3095 to confirm the amount before paying, since amounts and dates shift.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Collect the latest tax notice, the receipt from your most recent payment and any assessment notice you received. Those papers show your values, your rate and the address the county has on file. If you recently bought the house, have the recorded deed ready, since a new owner needs a legal residence application of their own.

Phone the offices in a sensible order. The Assessor can tell you about the legal residence rate and address records, the Auditor covers the homestead exemption and the bill calculation, and Delinquent Tax Collection gives payoff amounts. Write down each answer with the date so your closing agent can rely on it.

If the house is vacant, rented or inherited, say so on the first call. Those situations affect who must file a legal residence application and who receives the bill, and the answer is easier to fix before a closing date is set than after it. A cash sale can close on your timeline and skips the repair list a retail buyer would send.

sections.h2: Selling a Florence County house with tax owed
sections.html:
Owing tax and selling the house can happen together. The title company can settle the balance from proceeds, provided the payoff figure is current.

  1. Call Delinquent Tax Collection, 843-665-3095, and ask for the payoff.
  2. Have the Assessor confirm the mailing address and your legal residence status.
  3. Look up the parcel on qPublic and check the lot's flood status before listing.
  4. If you manage the sale from out of town, Florence Regional Airport and the meeting of I-20 and I-95 keep the city easy to reach.

faqs.q: What is the Florence County property tax penalty schedule?
faqs.a: Missing January 15 brings 3 percent on January 16. Another 7 percent follows on February 2 and 5 percent more on March 17, totaling 15 percent plus collection costs.

faqs.q: Can I make a partial property tax payment in Florence County?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer must take the whole amount on the notice, penalties included, so a partial payment is refused.

faqs.q: Where is the Florence County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: Visit 180 N Irby Street in Florence or call 843-665-3041. Mailed payments go to P.O. Box 100501, Florence, SC 29502-0501.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a Florence County tax sale property?
faqs.a: One year and a day after the sale, for the owner or a mortgage holder, with interest added quarter by quarter.

faqs.q: Who handles appeals in Florence County?
faqs.a: Appeals go to the Tax Assessor and must be in writing, within 90 days after a notice is mailed. The current form is available at 843-665-3056.
